lines: Rent went up again this month. Apparently living under a shield counts as a luxury amenity now.
Did you walk here from outside the shield, in that? You must be freezing in all that metal.
I just want one morning where the train is on time and nobody mentions the monsters.
Nice armour. Is that for a costume party, or are things really that bad out there?
My neighbour swears the shield hums louder at night. I sleep with the window shut anyway.
Excuse me, you are standing in the crosswalk. The cars here will not wait forever.
Coffee prices doubled since the last outage. Somebody upstairs is making a fortune off our nerves.
I moved here for the safety. Nobody mentioned the safety comes with a three-year lease.
Is it true people outside still cook over open fires? That sounds oddly relaxing, honestly.
Please do not swing that sword near my car. The insurance forms alone would ruin my week.
Lovely day, isn't it? Well, the sky is filtered through a glowing dome, but still lovely.
They say the corporation keeps the lights on. I just wish they would keep the elevators running too.
Another visitor from the old lands. Do you people ever knock, or do you just wander in?
My screen says it will rain today. Funny, the rain never quite reaches us through the shield.
I work nights, I sleep days, and I have not seen the actual sun in months.
You look lost. The bus stop is that way, but I doubt they take gold coins.
My kid wants a sword now, thanks to you. I hope you are proud of yourself.
Some days I think about leaving. Then I remember what howls past the shield after dark.
The landlord fixed the heating, finally. I suspect it was an accident, but I will take it.
Have you seen the research building at night? Those blinking red lights make my skin crawl.
I used to think the shield was a miracle. Now it just feels like a very expensive lid.
Do not mind me, I am late for a meeting about another meeting.
Everyone here has a theory about what Kratos does in that building. Mine is that I do not ask.
Is that real blood on your boots? Please do not track it into the lobby.
I tried a sword-fighting class once. I lasted ten minutes and pulled a muscle.
The news says everything is fine. The news always says everything is fine.
If you are selling something, I already have three subscriptions I cannot cancel.
Welcome, I guess. Try the noodle place on the corner, it is the only honest business left.
My grandmother remembers when this was all fields. Then the shield came, and the towers followed.
Sometimes the shield flickers and the whole street goes quiet, waiting. Then everyone pretends nothing happened.
I have lived here twelve years and never once spoken to my neighbours. It is wonderfully peaceful.
Do you not have a phone? Then how do you people ever find each other?
They raised the parking fees again. At this rate I will be riding a horse like you.
Careful at the crossing, the lights change whenever they feel like it.
Third double shift this week. My manager calls it a growth opportunity, and I call it a hostage situation.
The printer on the fourteenth floor jammed again. I swear it does it out of spite.
If anyone asks, I have been on a coffee break for exactly five minutes.
I fix the street lights. Every night something out past the shield stares back at them.
Quarterly reports are due tomorrow and my screen just froze. Wonderful, absolutely wonderful.
They gave us a pizza party instead of a raise. The pizza was cold.
I mop the lobby floors every night. You would not believe what people leave behind.
My badge stopped working this morning. Either a glitch, or I am about to be let go.
Overtime again. At least the vending machine downstairs still likes me.
Do you need something filed? If not, please stop standing between me and the elevator.
We are not allowed to talk about the deliveries to the research building. So I will not.
Somebody rerouted the air ducts again, and now the whole floor smells like burnt toast.
I have a meeting at nine, a call at ten, and a breakdown pencilled in for noon.
The pipes under this street are older than the towers. Nobody wants to pay to replace them.
My supervisor sends messages at midnight, and I answer them at midnight. That is my life now.
Hey, you are not on the visitor list. I am not going to report you, I just noticed.
I came here to be an architect. Now I calibrate the shield's relay boxes, twelve hours a day.
Want some advice? Never volunteer for the late shift at the research facility, never.
Elevator four is broken again. I put up a sign, and somebody stole the sign.
The new software update deleted my whole week of work. Nobody upstairs seems surprised.
I retire in four years, seven months and nine days. Not that I am counting.
Every desk in my office faces a wall. They call it focus design; I call it a cubicle.
You carry a sword to work? Honestly, some mornings I would like one too.
I replaced six shield panels this month. Something keeps scratching at them from the outside.
Lunch is a sandwich at my desk while I answer complaints about other people's lunches.
They installed a coffee machine that tells me to have a productive day. I hate it.
The building's heating is on in summer and off in winter. Nobody knows who controls it.
I sign forms that approve other forms. Somewhere, I hope, someone actually does something.
Annual review next week. I plan to smile, nod, and update my resume that evening.
We got a memo saying morale is mandatory. Attendance at the morale meeting, too.
I clean the windows on the sixtieth floor. From up there the monsters look like ants.
My cousin works in the research building. She stopped coming to family dinners.
Do not touch that panel. It is either a light switch or an alarm, and nobody remembers which.
Five more minutes on my break, then back to pretending spreadsheets matter.
Kratos security. Keep moving, and keep that blade sheathed inside city limits.
I signed up for good pay and a pension. Nobody said anything about monsters.
Eyes forward, civilian. Whatever you saw past the shield, you did not see it.
Our rifles outrange your sword by a good half mile. Just a friendly reminder.
Twelve-hour patrols, and the coffee in the barracks tastes like engine oil.
Command says the perimeter is secure. Command does not walk the perimeter at night.
Interesting armour, is it hand-forged? We just get ours out of a supply catalogue.
If you are heading for the research facility, turn around. That is a direct order, mostly.
I have seen things carried out of that facility that the reports describe as equipment.
Stay out of restricted zones. They are clearly marked with signs, fences and very bored snipers.
My squad leader thinks you outsiders are spies. I think you just took a wrong turn.
Some of my unit went down into the fortress last month. Only half came back.
The pay and the dental plan are excellent. The nightmares, sadly, are not covered.
Do not mistake our politeness for patience. We are paid to be polite, not patient.
I would ask where you got that sword, but caring is above my clearance.
We are corporate security, not the city watch. Report your stolen goods to someone else.
Every night something tests the shield on the north side. Every night we pretend it is wind.
Keep your hands visible. Not because I suspect you, but because the cameras like it.
Back in training they never mentioned we would be fighting things with too many teeth.
You look capable. If you ever want a contract, the recruiting office has excellent coffee.
Mind your step near the checkpoint. The floor sensors are very sensitive and very loud.
Orders change every hour. Right now my orders are to stand here and look stern.
That research building does not exist, officially. I guard it anyway, every single day.
I miss real weather. Rain on a helmet sounds better than the shield's endless humming.
Three more years and my contract is up. Then I am buying a farm somewhere far away.
Do you hear that? If you ever do, run toward us, not away.
My sergeant says magic is just technology nobody has written a manual for yet.
We have orders not to engage outsiders unless provoked. Please do not provoke anyone.
Ammunition counts are due at dusk. If one round is missing, I fill in forms for a week.
The defenders in the lower halls do not answer to us anymore. Nobody will tell me why.
Nice day for a patrol. Every day is a nice day under the dome, unfortunately.
Stand clear of the vehicle lane. The supply trucks do not brake for swords.
I have a family across town. That is why I hold this line, whatever the board decides.
They told us the outsiders are primitive. You do not look primitive, you look dangerous.
Badge, please. No badge means the lobby is as far as you go.
Sign the visitor log. Your full name, not whatever title they gave you outside.
I watch thirty cameras all night. Mostly I watch people forgetting their keycards.
Weapons are not permitted past this desk. Yes, that includes the glowing one.
The gate closes at ten sharp. After that, you sleep wherever the shield lets you.
I have stood at this door for nine years. Not one person has ever said thank you.
You need an appointment to see anyone upstairs. The next opening is in three weeks.
If the alarm sounds, do not panic. Well, panic quietly, and toward the stairwell.
The elevator to the top floors needs a key I am not allowed to hold.
Please remove your helmet for the camera. Thank you, now I have something to frown at.
Deliveries go around the back. Swords, apparently, come through the front.
Someone tried to climb the outer wall last week. The wall won, in the end.
My shift ends at dawn and my relief is always late. I have accepted this as fate.
That door behind me stays locked. I do not know what is behind it, and I like that.
Visiting hours ended at five. Unless you are here to fix the coffee machine, of course.
Do not lean on the glass. It is bulletproof, but my patience certainly is not.
Lost and found is on the second floor. Last month someone left a crossbow there.
They tell us to be courteous to outsiders. So, courteously: please step back from the barrier.
The research facility's guards earn double what we do. Then again, they rarely sleep.
Every night at three, the lights on the security floor flicker. Maintenance says it is normal.
I checked your name against the list and you are not on it. Nobody ever is.
Metal detector, please. Oh, never mind, you are almost entirely metal, are you not?
I have had this chair since my first day. It squeaks, but it is loyal.
No loitering in the lobby. Standing still for too long counts as loitering here.
The gate scanners cannot read whatever you are carrying. That makes my supervisor nervous.
Keep to the marked path inside the building. The unmarked ones end in locked rooms.
Some nights I hear knocking from inside the walls. I write it down as plumbing.
Your boots are muddy. The cleaning crew will hate you, and they will blame me.
I used to work the city gate, and now I work a door. Promotion, they said.
Please wait here. Someone with more authority and less patience will be down shortly.
You look like trouble. Nothing personal, it is my job to think everyone looks like trouble.
Fire exits are clearly marked. Monster exits, unfortunately, are not.
If you need the bathroom, it requires a pass. The pass requires a form.
The cameras saw you come through the shield. The cameras see everything, eventually.
Neighbourhood watch. We do not have guns, but we do have very bright flashlights.
We meet every second evening in the laundromat. There are snacks, if you want to join.
Corporate security only guards their buildings. Somebody has to look after the rest of us.
I keep a heavy bat by my door. It has never met a monster, but it is ready.
Did you see anyone suspicious on Seventh Street? Anyone besides yourself, I mean.
We walk the blocks after dark in pairs. Nobody walks alone since the shield flickered.
My reflective vest is not armour, but it makes me feel braver than I am.
Write down anything strange. Strange noises, strange lights, strange women in old armour.
We petitioned the council for more street lights. They sent us a survey.
If a shield panel goes dark, we call it in. Then we wait, and we pray a little.
I am an accountant by day. By night, I patrol with a whistle and a clipboard.
Somebody has been leaving claw marks on the garage doors near the east wall.
We do not trust Kratos, and Kratos does not trust us. It is a very honest arrangement.
You can fight, can you not? We could use someone like you on the night rota.
The radio crackles every time we pass the research building. We have stopped walking that way.
Our group chat has two hundred members, and three of them actually show up.
Last week we caught a raccoon in the bins. We celebrated like it was a dragon.
Keep your door locked, keep your lights on, and keep your neighbours' numbers handy.
The patrol cars drive straight past our street. So we patrol it ourselves, on foot.
I joined after my brother's shop was broken into. The police never even came.
We have a map with every dark alley marked in red. It is mostly red now.
Do you know old-fashioned first aid? Ours is mostly from instructional videos.
Something scratched at the shield near the old playground last night. We all heard it.
Watch meeting tonight, we are voting on new torches. The flashlight kind, not the fire kind.
Some say we are just nosy neighbours with whistles. They are not entirely wrong.
My wife thinks this is a phase. It has been six years.
Stay on the lit side of the street. The dark side has had too many incidents.
If you hear three short whistles, that is us. If you hear a long howl, that is not.
We are building a shelter in the community centre basement. Just in case the shield fails.
You walked in from the wilds alone? That is brave, or very foolish, probably both.
I asked corporate security for help once. They asked if I had an appointment.
Our motto is see something, say something. Lately we see far too much.
Every volunteer gets a vest, a whistle and a lifetime of poor sleep.
Tell us if you see anything crawling near the drains. We have been hearing things.
Is that a real sword? Can I touch it just once, I promise I will not tell!
My teacher says people outside the shield live in castles. Do you live in a castle?
I am not supposed to talk to strangers. But you are not a stranger, you are a knight.
When I grow up I want to fight monsters, or be a dentist. I have not decided.
My tablet died and now I have to play outside. It is the worst day ever.
Mom says the shield keeps the monsters out. I think the monsters just have not tried hard enough.
Do you have a dragon? Everyone at school says outsiders have dragons.
I drew you a picture of the shield. The purple bits are the scary parts.
Can you do magic? Make my homework disappear, please, pretty please?
My brother says the big glass building eats people. He is lying, right?
Why does your armour not have buttons? How do you get it off for bedtime?
I saw a car stop for a pigeon today. The pigeon did not even say thank you.
We had a shield drill at school and hid under our desks for twenty minutes. It was boring.
You smell like a campfire, that is so cool. Our apartment smells like carpet.
Bet you cannot beat me in a race to the bus stop. Ready, set, go!
My dad works at the big research place. He never says what he does there.
If I give you my lunch money, will you teach me sword tricks?
I am a spy, so you did not see me. Pretend you did not see me.
Is it scary outside the shield? I want to see a real tree, a big wild one.
My friend says if you touch the shield your hair stands up. I want to try.
I am collecting bottle caps and I have three hundred and twelve. Do you have any?
Grown-ups keep saying everything is fine. That is what they say when it is not fine.
I can count all the way to a thousand. Do you want to hear me do it?
You talk funny, not bad funny. Funny like somebody in a story.
My hamster escaped. If you see a little brown monster, that is just Biscuit.
School is closed today because the shield made a weird noise. Best day ever!
Do knights have to do homework? Because if not, I am becoming a knight.
I heard a growl from the drain by my building. Mom said it was the pipes.
Can I wear your helmet? I will give it back, probably.
My grandpa says he saw a real horse once. Do you have a horse, and is it nice?
The ice cream truck stopped coming because of the monsters, Mom says. I hate monsters.
You are way cooler than the security guards. They never smile and they never wave.
I built a fort out of couch cushions. It has a shield too, made of a blanket.
At night I count the red lights on the tall towers until I fall asleep.
He went to work in the research building one morning. They sent his badge back in a box.
I bring fresh flowers every week. The plastic ones look wrong, somehow.
Please be quiet for a moment. This is the only place in the city that is quiet.
She always said the shield would protect us. It did not protect her.
They never told us what happened in the lower halls. Just the word accident, and a form to sign.
I keep calling his number just to hear his voice on the message.
Forty names on this wall, and the corporation sent one wreath for all of them.
Do people outside the shield grieve the same way? I hope it is kinder there.
He was a security officer. Brave, stubborn, and terrible at saying goodbye.
I sit here every lunch break. It is the only hour of the day I feel honest.
The compensation cheque arrived today. I would burn it if I thought it would help.
My son was nine. The shield flickered for a single minute, and that was all it took.
You look like someone who has buried friends too. I am sorry for whatever you lost.
They will build another tower on this spot one day. I hope someone remembers us then.
I still set two cups out for coffee every morning. I cannot stop myself.
The candles keep going out in the draft from the vents. I keep lighting them again.
She worked overtime for six years so we could afford this city. Now I am alone in it.
Some days I am angry, some days I am just tired. Today I am both.
If you ever go down into that fortress, remember the people who never came back up.
The memorial was supposed to be bigger. The budget was cut in a meeting I was not invited to.
I talk to her photograph every evening. It does not answer, but it listens better than most.
Everyone says time heals. It has been three years and time has done nothing.
Thank you for stopping. Most people walk past this wall without looking up from their screens.
My brother was in the neighbourhood watch. He went out one night after a noise and never came home.
I used to hate the shield's humming. Now it reminds me of the night he left.
They engraved his name wrong. I have filed four requests to fix it.
Grief is strange under a dome. The sky never changes, so the days all blur together.
I keep asking the director why the families were never told the truth. She never answers.
I do not cry anymore. I just come here and stand until my legs ache.
We were going to leave the city next spring. We had the tickets and everything.
The flowers wilt so fast in here. Nothing living seems to last long under the shield.
My daughter keeps asking when Daddy is coming home. I have run out of answers.
Every name on this wall had a desk, a coffee mug, and a family waiting at home.
Sit with me a while, if you have a moment. It is easier with someone here.
The traffic lights are talking to each other. Green means yes, red means they know.
I have counted every pigeon in this city, and there is one too many. One too many!
Psst, the shield is actually a giant soap bubble. Do not poke it, whatever you do.
Did you come out of a painting? You look like you came out of a painting.
My toaster predicted the last blackout. Nobody believed my toaster, nobody ever does.
I live in the bus shelter now, very modern. Excellent views of the bin.
The glass building hums a little song at night. I have learned all the words.
Do you want to buy a rock? It is a very important rock, and it knows things.
Cars are just horses that forgot how to eat grass. I read that somewhere, or dreamt it.
They put something in the tap water to make us love spreadsheets. I drink only rain.
You there, metal lady, have you seen my left shoe? It ran off on its own.
I asked the shield a question yesterday and it answered in purple. I am still thinking about it.
Every escalator in this city secretly goes down. Even the ones that look like they go up.
I used to be a banker. Then I saw the numbers move by themselves, and I left.
The moon is fake, they painted it on the inside of the dome. I checked.
Hello, hello, hello! I am practising my greetings for when the monsters arrive.
My cat runs this street, unofficially. Do not tell the council, they get jealous.
I am building a shield of my own out of tinfoil and bottle caps. Nearly finished.
If you hum backwards, the street lights turn blue. Try it, or are you a coward?
The research people took my dreams. Now I dream about filing cabinets every night.
Ah, a knight, I knew it! The prophecy in my cereal box was right.
I have been waiting for the bus for eleven years. It will come, it has to.
Do not walk on the white stripes! They are for the ghosts to cross the road.
I once shook hands with a robot. It had a very weak grip and no sense of humour.
Want to hear a secret? The fountain in the square grants wishes backwards, so keep your coins.
Ha, swords! Everybody knows the real weapon is a sharp, well-timed remark.
Monsters do not frighten me, paperwork does. Monsters never ask for a signature.
They keep painting over my drawings under the bridge. My drawings are warnings, you know.
I collect sounds in jars, and this one is the shield sneezing. Want to listen?
Have you noticed the office people walk in perfect lines? Like ants with briefcases.
When the dome falls, I will be ready. I have three umbrellas.
I talk to the vending machines. They are very lonely, and very misunderstood.
Are you real? Pinch me, no, pinch yourself, somebody pinch somebody, quickly!
Last night the street lights winked at me, all of them, in order. It was beautiful.
Repent! The shield will not hold forever, and neither will your savings.
They built towers to the sky, but the sky does not want them. Mark my words.
You worship your screens and your salaries. What will they buy you when the dome cracks?
The red lights on the research building are eyes, friends. And they are watching you.
An armoured stranger walks among us! Surely a sign that the end draws near.
Hear me! What the corporation digs up below the city, it cannot bury again.
The monsters at the shield are not outside. They are a mirror of what we have become.
Throw down your keycards! Walk out into the wilds and beg the old world for mercy.
Every overtime hour is a stone in the wall of your own tomb!
The shield hums because it is tired. Even it knows it cannot hold back judgement.
Do not look away from me, office drone! The reckoning has no lunch break.
When the lights go dark, the meek will inherit the elevators. And the stairs.
You, stranger, you come from the old lands. Tell them our glass towers are already falling.
The fortress beneath that facility is a door, friends. Doors open both ways!
Your rent rises and your hope falls. Is that not the clearest sign of all?
I have seen it in a vision: a city of light, swallowed whole by the dark beyond.
They promised you safety. Safety is a word written on a cage.
The end is near! The end has been near for years, but this time I mean it.
Turn off your screens and listen! Can you not hear the scratching at the dome?
The machines below do not sleep, they wait. And what waits, eventually acts.
Heaven, they call it. A heaven with a lease agreement and a security deposit!
Brothers and sisters, the shield is not a blessing. It is a ransom, paid monthly.
The old gods walk the wilds still. You built this place to hide from them.
Every car that passes is a chariot with no destination. Think on that, commuters!
Look at her armour! The past has come to judge us, sword in hand!
I was once like you, a clerk with a badge. Then the dreams began.
Confess your sins now, friends, while the street lights still work.
The corporation counts its profits while the monsters count the cracks. Who is counting faster?
They will tell you I am mad. Ask yourselves why they are so eager to say so.
The day is coming when the dome goes dark and every door in this city opens.
Your coffee will not save you, your promotion will not save you! Nothing you own will save you!
Give me one minute of your commute and I will give you eternity. Fair trade, friends.
What they build inside that glass block walks on two legs and carries a rifle. Remember I said so.
Pray hard, friends, and pray quickly. The shield is listening, and so is the dark.
What will it be? We have beer, wine, and something blue the chemists drink.
First time in a real bar? You look like you are used to drinking from a horn.
Happy hour starts at five. In this city, it is the only happy hour anyone gets.
Leave the sword by the door, please. Last time someone swung one, I lost three bottles.
The overtime crowd comes in at midnight. Quiet drinkers, big tippers, very sad eyes.
I hear every rumour in this city across this counter. Most of them are about Kratos.
Our house special is called the Shield Breaker. Two of those and you will see sparks too.
Do outsiders pay in gold? I have never held real gold, so let me look at it first.
Pull up a stool. You look like you have walked a hundred miles in those boots.
The bar closes when the last customer falls asleep. Usually that is around three.
The facility's guards drink here off duty and never talk about work. They drink like they want to forget.
Ice and lemon? Or do people out in the wilds just drink it warm and angry?
I wipe this counter forty times a night. It has never once been clean.
That table in the corner is reserved for the security chief's crew. Do not sit there.
You want food? We have bar snacks, salty, crunchy and slightly older than you would think.
Every night someone cries into a drink over a lost job. Tonight it might be me.
The music is too loud, I know, but it drowns out the shield's humming. People pay for that.
Rough day? The first one is on the house, and the second one is on you.
I used to tend bar in a hotel near the top floors. Better tips, worse company.
A mead? I think I have one dusty bottle somewhere, bought as a joke years ago.
Do not start fights in here. I have a bat behind the counter and a very short temper.
Regulars come in, sit in the same seats, order the same drinks. It is like a ritual.
If you hear about any work out past the shield, the folks at the back table are hiring.
Last call is when I say it is. Tonight, I am feeling generous.
Office folks drink to forget their bosses, soldiers to forget the fortress. What about you?
You tip in coins with faces I have never seen. I will take them anyway.
The power went out last week and we kept pouring by candlelight. Best night we ever had.
I mix a drink for every mood. Yours looks like it needs something strong and quiet.
Glass of water? Sure, filtered three times, tastes like nothing, very modern.
People tell bartenders everything. Trust me, you do not want to know what this city confesses.
Careful with that one. It is called the Overtime, and it hits you just as hard.
I keep the screens off in here. Nobody needs the news while they drink.
Sit anywhere except the stool by the window. That one wobbles, and so do its customers.
Come back any time. The drinks are cheap, the chairs are soft, and nobody asks questions.
